newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha edges up, spreads unchanged at even.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha edges up, spreads unchanged at even.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha was a little firmer in afternoon trade on Thursday, mirroring moderate gains in crude oil markets overnight, traders said.
However, most market participants kept to the sidelines due to uncertainty over crude's direction, they added.
Asia's benchmark forward contract open-spec naphtha was assessed at $207.50/208.50 per tonne for both second-half September and first-half October delivery.
The second-half September contract was bought by a South Korean trader at $207.00 in late afternoon dealing on Wednesday. The seller was said to be a Western trading house.
In spreads, second-half September/second-half October was indicated at minus 25 cents/plus 25 cents.
In middle distillates, traders said they believed some Japanese oil firms would soon start kerosene term talks with South Korean and Middle Eastern suppliers for the winter heating season.

Oil firms in Japan usually step up kerosene imports towards the winter to pile up stocks for the peak heating season, while adjusting their refinery yields from maximum gas oil production to maximum kerosene output, they said.
